section: 1.  Identify the most‐recent date tag among saved CSVs
grain_in: one row per CSV file in results/ matching the date-tagged pattern
grain_out: one row per base name (nine at most), holding the path of the file chosen for it
operation: Lists files in results/ whose names match one of nine hard-coded base names followed by a YYYY-MM-DD tag, parses base and date out of each filename, and keeps one file per base: newest date first, ties broken by descending filename. The tibble construction, the redundant filter on base %in% base_names, and the ungroup are absorbed because they only carry the parsed fields into the slice; base_names and file_regex sit inside the region because they are the settings that decide which files enter the analysis at all.
settings: Nine base names listed literally; regex anchors an exact _YYYY-MM-DD.csv suffix, so any other naming is invisible; arrange(base, desc(date), desc(fname)) then slice_head(n = 1), so a same-date tie is broken by the lexicographically largest filename; date taken by as.Date on the first YYYY-MM-DD substring.
na_behavior: A base with no matching file simply yields no row; that case is reported only by the warning() below the region, which does not stop the script, so the failure surfaces later as a missing object. A filename whose date fails to parse gives NA date, which desc() sorts last, so such a file is picked only when it is the sole candidate; unparseable dates and merely older files are not distinguishable downstream.

section: 2. Read each latest file into a named list
grain_in: one row per base name (a path)
grain_out: a named list of tables, one element per base, each keeping the grain of its own file; only portfolio_ps and L5_alpha_diversity_observed are used later in this script
units_out: mixed, as stored in each file
operation: Reads each selected file with readr::read_csv and deframes the result into a list keyed by base name. The list2env call and the renames below it (alpha_div, gamma_div, portfolio, and so on, through com_inv) are renames, so they are not nodes and fall outside every region; the rm() that follows keeps only the renamed objects plus P and script_dir. Seven of the nine tables are read and renamed but never used again in this script.
settings: show_col_types = FALSE; no col_types given, so every column type is guessed by readr from the first rows of each file; no explicit encoding or NA-string argument.
na_behavior: Empty fields and the default NA strings become NA. Parsing problems raise a warning but are never inspected with problems(), and a column whose type is guessed wrongly turns into character or NA silently, which cannot be told apart from genuinely missing data later.

grain_in: one row of portfolio_ps, believed to be major_area x period x season; this cannot be confirmed from this script
grain_out: same grain, restricted to rows with a finite positive portfolio value and a parseable period
units_out: log10 ratio, plus a mid-period year in calendar years
operation: Derives period_num from the numeric part of the period label, sets period_mid = 1991 + 3 * period_num, coerces season and major_area to factors, log10-transforms portfolio where it is finite and positive, then filters to rows where port_t, period_mid, season and major_area are all present. Code and comment disagree about period_mid: the header above says P1 covers 1992 to 1994 with a midpoint near 1993, but the formula returns 1994 for P1, that is the last year of the bin rather than its middle. The factor coercions and the period parsing are absorbed because they only feed the filter and the models; the threshold and the filter are the decisions.
settings: Keep only portfolio > 0 and is.finite(portfolio); log base 10; period_mid = 1991 + 3 * period_num; factor levels default to sorted unique values, so the reference level for season and major_area is whichever sorts first; sub("^P", "", period) assumes every label starts with P.
na_behavior: Portfolio values that are NA, NaN, Inf, exactly zero, or negative all collapse into one NA_real_ in port_t and are then removed by the filter; the five causes are not distinguishable afterwards and the number of rows dropped is never recorded. A period label not of the form P<number> gives NA period_num and NA period_mid, and the row leaves through the same filter, so a labelling problem looks identical to a nonpositive portfolio value.
notes: Looks like the mid year is offset by one, but it should not affect the qualitative results!

grain_out: one fitted model, printed as one coefficient and smooth table
units_out: coefficients on the log10 scale, effective degrees of freedom, p-values
operation: Fits a generalized additive model of log10 portfolio effect on a smooth of mid-period year with additive fixed effects for season and major_area, and prints the summary. The print is absorbed because it only reports the fit.
settings: k = 6 basis dimension on the period_mid smooth, default thin-plate basis; method = REML; gaussian family by default; season and major_area enter as fixed factors, not random effects, so bay-level dependence is not modelled; no autocorrelation term across periods within a bay.
na_behavior: port_clean has already removed missing values, so the default na.action never fires and no row is silently dropped here. If port_clean held fewer than 6 distinct period_mid values, gam would error rather than return a missing result.

start_anchor: dat_lin <- port_clean %>% mutate(t_c = as.numeric(scale(period_mid, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)))
grain_out: one fitted model, of which only the centred-time row of the coefficient table is printed
units_out: slope in log10 ratio per year, with SE, t and p
operation: Centres period_mid on its own mean and fits a linear trend in log10 portfolio effect controlling for season and major_area, then prints only the t_c row. The centring mutate is absorbed because it only rescales the predictor for this fit. No correlation or weights argument is supplied, so gls here is ordinary least squares with REML variance estimation despite the use of nlme. The region also ends one line later than the anchor shows: its true last line, print(summary(m_lin)$tTable["t_c", , drop = FALSE]), carries a trailing comment and so cannot serve as an end_anchor.
settings: scale(center = TRUE, scale = FALSE), so the origin of t_c is the sample mean of period_mid within port_clean and not a fixed calendar year, which makes the intercept depend on which rows survived the upstream filter; method = REML; no correlation structure; only the t_c row is reported, so the season and bay estimates are computed but never shown.
na_behavior: No missing values remain after the upstream filter. If t_c were absent from the table, the subset by name would error rather than yield NA.

start_anchor: fig_port_time <- ggplot(port_clean, aes(x = period_mid, y = port_t)) +
grain_out: one figure, plus a second GAM fit computed inside it
operation: Plots log10 portfolio effect against mid-period year and overlays a GAM smooth fitted inside geom_smooth with the same k = 6 but with no season or major_area terms, so the drawn curve and its band are a separate fit and not the partial effect from the model above; then writes the TIFF and prints the plot. The ggsave, the print, and the reassignment of results_dir to the path it already had are absorbed because they only render or relocate the same object. Unlike the diversity figures below, this one is drawn whether or not P equals 1.
settings: Smooth formula y ~ s(x, k = 6) with method gam; se = TRUE, giving a 95% band; points at alpha 0.5; output 16 x 10 cm at 600 dpi, TIFF with LZW compression, written to results/S3_fig_PORTFOLIO_time.tif and overwritten without warning if present.
na_behavior: No missing values remain in these columns, so geom_point and geom_smooth drop nothing and no removed-rows warning can appear.

grain_in: one row of portfolio_ps joined against one row of alpha diversity, both believed to be major_area x period x season
grain_out: bay x period x season with richness and shannon attached, restricted to rows where all three are present; if alpha_div holds more than one row per key the join multiplies rows and the grain changes, which this script never checks
units_in: ratio (portfolio effect); species count and Shannon diversity
units_out: log10 ratio alongside a count and a diversity index
operation: Renames portfolio to portfolio_effect, left-joins alpha diversity by major_area, period and season, log10-transforms the portfolio effect, and drops rows missing port_t, richness or shannon. This restarts from the raw portfolio table rather than from port_clean, so it is a second population, filtered on its own terms and carrying no period_mid; the two populations need not contain the same rows. The rename is absorbed; the join and the drop are the decisions. Open question: does alpha_div have exactly one row per major_area x period x season, and are its period labels coded the same way as the portfolio table?
settings: left_join by major_area, period and season, so portfolio rows with no diversity match are kept and then dropped at the next step; keep only portfolio_effect > 0 and finite; log base 10; drop_na applied to port_t, richness and shannon only, so other columns may still be missing.
na_behavior: As in port_clean, NA, NaN, Inf, zero and negative portfolio values all become one NA and leave together. On top of that, a key absent from alpha_div yields NA richness and shannon from the left join and is removed by the same drop_na, so a failed join and a genuinely missing diversity value are indistinguishable; the number of unmatched keys is never counted.

units_out: slope in log10 ratio per species, plus variance components
operation: Fits a linear mixed model of log10 portfolio effect on richness with crossed random intercepts for bay and season. The summary is printed further down, outside this region, along with those of the other two models.
settings: Fixed effect richness only; random intercepts for major_area and season, no random slopes; lmer default REML = TRUE; lmerTest is attached, so the printed summary carries Satterthwaite degrees of freedom; period is not in the model, so the time trend fitted above is not controlled for here.
na_behavior: No missing values remain after drop_na, so no rows are dropped by na.action. Season has few levels, so its variance component can be estimated at or near zero and the fit reported as singular; that warning prints to the console but is not captured or acted on, and a zero variance is not distinguishable in the stored object from a genuinely negligible one.

units_out: slope in log10 ratio per unit of Shannon diversity, plus variance components
operation: Fits the same mixed model structure as the richness model but with shannon as the single predictor, on the same rows. It is a separate node because the predictor, and therefore the quantity reported, differs.
settings: Fixed effect shannon only; random intercepts for major_area and season; REML by default; the diversity metric is whichever column alpha_div names shannon, and whether it is the index or its exponential (Hill number q = 1) cannot be told from this script.
na_behavior: Same as the richness model: nothing left to drop, and a singular fit for season would print a warning that is not captured.

units_in: log10 ratio, species count, Shannon diversity
units_out: two partial slopes on the log10 scale, plus variance components
operation: Fits richness and shannon together in one mixed model, so both coefficients become partial effects conditional on the other. Richness and Shannon diversity are usually strongly correlated and no collinearity check is run, so the two slopes here are not comparable with the single-predictor slopes above. The three cat and print lines that follow the region report all three models and belong to no node.
settings: Fixed effects richness and shannon; random intercepts for major_area and season; REML by default; no centring or scaling of either predictor, so the intercept refers to zero richness and zero Shannon diversity.
na_behavior: Nothing left to drop after drop_na. If the two predictors were collinear enough to be rank deficient, lmer would drop one and report it in the summary rather than return a missing value.

grain_out: one two-panel figure, plus two OLS fits computed inside it
units_in: log10 ratio, species count, Shannon diversity
units_out: log10 ratio against a count and against a diversity index
operation: Builds one scatterplot of log10 portfolio effect against richness and one against shannon, each with a straight-line smooth fitted by ordinary least squares that ignores the bay and season random effects, combines them with patchwork, prints, and saves. The lines drawn are therefore separate fits from the mixed models and their slopes need not match the fixed effects reported above. The ggsave call sits outside the if (P == 1) block, so with P = 0 the panels are never built and ggsave fails on a missing object; the region covers both because the save depends on the block. Two title arguments are commented out.
settings: Whole plotting block gated on P == 1 while the save is not; method = "lm" with se = TRUE, giving 95% bands; points at alpha 0.6; panels tagged a and b, richness above shannon; output 8.5 x 12 cm at 600 dpi, TIFF with LZW compression, to results/fig_2_PORTFOLIO_both.tif; results_dir reassigned to the path it already held.
na_behavior: No missing values remain in df_port_div, so no rows are silently dropped by the layers and no removed-rows warning can appear. If P is not 1, the failure is an error at ggsave rather than a missing figure.

grain_out: one pair of R2 values per model
operation: Computes marginal and conditional R2 for the three mixed models and prints them, but only when MuMIn is installed. The prints are absorbed because they only report. The closing brace of the if block on the next line is not used as end_anchor because a lone brace is not unique in the file.
settings: Guarded by requireNamespace("MuMIn"), so an absent package skips the whole block with no message and no output; r.squaredGLMM defaults are used, which for a gaussian lmer returns the delta-method marginal and conditional pair as a one-row matrix.
na_behavior: If a model is singular, the conditional R2 is computed from a zero variance component and comes back as a finite number that cannot be distinguished from a genuine estimate; no singularity check is run first. Where r.squaredGLMM cannot compute a value it returns NA in place, and NA is printed without stopping the script.

end_anchor: cat("  • 1 unit increase in Shannon multiplies PE by ~", round(log10_mult(fixef(m_shan_t)["shannon"]), 2), "x\n", sep = "")
units_in: log10 ratio per unit of Shannon diversity
units_out: multiplier on the portfolio effect per unit of Shannon diversity
operation: Defines log10_mult, which raises 10 to a coefficient, and applies it to the shannon fixed effect to state how much a one-unit rise in Shannon diversity multiplies the portfolio effect. The definition sits in this region; the second call site is the next node, because the model it draws from differs.
settings: Point estimate only, with no confidence interval carried through the back-transformation; rounded to 2 decimal places; the coefficient is taken from the single-predictor Shannon model, not from the combined model.
na_behavior: fixef(m_shan_t)["shannon"] returns NA if that name is absent, 10^NA is NA, and cat prints NA without any error, so a renamed or missing coefficient looks the same as a computed result of NA.

start_anchor: cat("  • +1 species multiplies PE by ~", round(log10_mult(fixef(m_rich_t)["richness"]), 3), "x\n", sep = "")
end_anchor: cat("  • +1 species multiplies PE by ~", round(log10_mult(fixef(m_rich_t)["richness"]), 3), "x\n", sep = "")
units_out: multiplier on the portfolio effect per added species
operation: Second call site of log10_mult, applied to the richness fixed effect to state the multiplier per added species. It is a separate node from the definition above because the input model is different.
settings: Point estimate only, no interval; rounded to 3 decimal places, unlike the 2 used for Shannon; taken from the single-predictor richness model.
na_behavior: As above, a missing or renamed richness coefficient yields NA, which prints without error and is indistinguishable from a real NA result.

grain_in: one row per major_area x period x season
grain_out: one finite portfolio value per surviving row, pooled with no grouping
units_out: ratio (portfolio effect), and a count n
operation: Pulls the raw portfolio column out as a vector, keeps only finite values, and records how many are left. This is a third population, filtered differently from the two above: values at or below zero are kept here, while both model paths removed them, so the descriptive statistics below and the model estimates do not describe the same rows. Pooling also discards bay, period and season, so repeated observations of the same bay are treated as independent draws.
settings: is.finite as the only filter, with no positivity threshold and no grouping; the vector is taken from the raw portfolio object, not from port_clean or df_port_div.
na_behavior: NA, NaN, Inf and -Inf are all removed by the same test and cannot be told apart afterwards; the count of removed values is never recorded, since n counts only survivors.

grain_in: one finite portfolio value per row
grain_out: one median, mean, SE, bootstrap SE and interval for the whole pooled vector
units_out: ratio, and a ratio-scaled standard error and interval
operation: Computes the median, mean and standard error of the mean, then bootstraps the median with 10000 resamples and reports its standard deviation and a percentile interval. Descriptives and bootstrap sit in one region because they summarise the same pooled vector and the lines between them are comments and an intermediate vector of replicate medians that only carries the result forward.
settings: set.seed(2025) immediately before the bootstrap, so the interval is reproducible but conditional on that seed; B = 10000 resamples of size n with replacement; percentile interval at 0.025 and 0.975 through quantile with the default type 7; se_mean computed as sd/sqrt(n), which assumes the pooled rows are independent, though rows from one bay across seasons and periods are unlikely to be.
na_behavior: x is finite by construction, so median, mean and sd cannot be NA unless n is 0. With n equal to 0 the median and mean return NA, sd returns NA, every bootstrap replicate is NA, and se_med and ci_med come back NA and are reported without any error being raised.

grain_in: one finite portfolio value per row
grain_out: one test result for the pooled vector, and one printed summary list
units_out: a test statistic, a p-value, a one-sided interval and a pseudo-median on the ratio scale
operation: Runs a one-sided Wilcoxon signed rank test of the pooled portfolio values against 1, then assembles n, the descriptives, the bootstrap results and the test output into a list that is printed as the last statement of the script. The list is absorbed because it only carries results forward. Code and comment disagree on the last two entries: the comments describe conf_int and estimate as referring to (x - 1), but wilcox.test adds mu back before returning, so both are on the scale of x itself.
settings: mu = 1 as the null value; alternative = "greater", so the reported interval is one-sided with an infinite upper bound at conf.level = 0.95; exact = FALSE forces the normal approximation with continuity correction even where an exact test would be available; values exactly equal to 1 are dropped by the test and ties are handled by the approximation; the test treats the pooled rows as independent, as the SE above does.
na_behavior: x holds no missing values, so no observation is dropped for that reason. Ties and zero differences change the statistic silently rather than producing a missing value. An empty x errors rather than returning NA, so this path fails loudly instead of reporting a blank.
